title: Day 56 · Week 8, Day 0 — Body: the week the body gets measured — a raspberry growing a millimetre a day, the first bone, the gut that lives in the cord, and the one number that can move the due date
summary: Week 8 opens with the fifth Body episode. Your baby is at the turn from Carnegie stage 17 to 18 (11–17 mm; the NHS's 16 mm raspberry), growing close to a millimetre a day: pigmented eyes with eyelid folds beginning, the nasolacrimal groove, auricular hillocks merging into an ear, coronary arteries connecting to the aorta, a liver prominence, notches cutting between the finger rays, a thigh, an ankle and a foot plate, the lip fused. The first bone: the clavicle's shaft ossifies first, its two centres merging around post-fertilization day 45, with the femur (~day 43) and tibia (~day 44) behind it, and limb ossification starting at stage 18 (UNSW/Keibel & Mall). Physiological midgut herniation — the gut in the cord — in essentially every embryo at 10 weeks and 5% at 12 (Bogers 2019, 112 women, 699 scans), so the bump at the cord is normal. Why the NHS says 'fetus' at 8 weeks and this show says Day 70. Then the crown-rump length in full: Robinson & Fleming's 1975 Glasgow curve (±4.7 days), Hadlock 1992 (416 pregnancies, ±8%), INTERGROWTH-21st (4,607 women, 8 countries, SD ~2.4 days rising with length), ACOG Committee Opinion 700's ±5–7 days and its redating thresholds (>5 days before 9 weeks, >7 from 9 to 13+6), and the rule that the earliest good scan sets the date and later scans measure size, not age. What early scanning changes (Cochrane 2015: post-term induction RR 0.59 in 25,516 women; undetected twins RR 0.07; perinatal death RR 0.89, no difference). How often the measurement is taken wrong (Jakubowski 2020: 40% of 806 images rated accurate; neutral position the criterion that changes the date) and the one question to ask. The NHS 10–14-week scan and the 45–84 mm window. Tong 2008: 1.5% loss after a heartbeat at 8 weeks. And the first quantitative test of the thesis: in 1,631 Generation R pregnancies, smoking without folic acid cost 3.84 mm of crown-rump length by the dating scan, and the smallest fifth had 2.1× the odds of preterm birth, 2.4× low birth weight and 2.6× SGA (Mook-Kanamori 2010).
action: Ten minutes tonight with the Day 42 index card. On the back write 'CRL ___ mm, measured on Day ___, due date ___'. Find out which scan sets the date (this week's first visit or a later dating scan) and write that date on the Day 40 question sheet; if no scan is booked before Day 98, add question thirteen: will we have a dating scan before 14 weeks, and if not, why. At the scan, fill the blanks and ask one question: was the baby in a neutral position for that? Then write underneath: 'This is the due date. Later scans measure size, not age.'
